title: Pig Receiver

introduction.definition: A pig receiver is the trap at the downstream end of a pipeline section that catches the arriving pig and the debris it pushes. Flow is routed through the barrel so the pig is carried in; after it arrives, the trap is isolated, drained and depressurised, and the pig is removed through the closure door.
key_points: Barrel long enough for pig trains and debris
Check for hazardous deposits (pyrophoric iron sulphide, NORM) before opening
introduction.summary: A pig receiver is the trap at the downstream end of a pipeline section that catches the arriving pig. video_tutorials.title: Pig Receiver — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Pig Receiver.
A pig receiver is the trap at the downstream end of a pipeline section that catches the arriving pig and the debris it pushes.
Flow is routed through the barrel so the pig is carried in; after it arrives, the trap is isolated, drained and depressurised, and the pig is removed through the closure door.
Typical applications include oil, gas and product pipelines; slurry pipelines; pipeline cleaning and inspection campaigns.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Pig Receiver — Operation

script.narration: How the Pig Receiver works.
The trap valve is opened so flow passes through the barrel.
The arriving pig is carried through the reducer into the barrel.
Flow leaves via the outlet line back to the station.
The signaller confirms arrival; the trap is isolated, drained and vented.
The closure is opened and the pig and debris are removed.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Pig Receiver — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Pig Receiver.
Check closure seal and interlock.
Clean barrel and drains.
Inspect valves for seat damage from debris.
Watch for debris blocking drains: cannot drain trap. Common cause: wax, sludge.
Watch for pyrophoric fire on opening: smouldering debris. Common cause: iron sulphide exposed to air.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: What must be done before opening a receiver door?
options: Isolate, drain, depressurise and check for hazardous deposits

questions.question: Why might receiver debris be hazardous?
options: It may contain pyrophoric iron sulphide or NORM

questions.question: How does the pig enter the receiver?
options: Carried by the flow through the open trap valve
